l4_steps.name: Extract operational demand forecast from schedule system
l4_steps.output: Flight volume and frequency forecast by department
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ≥90% vs actuals at 6-month horizon
l4_steps.pain_point: Schedule changes in SkyWORKS are not auto-pushed to HR systems; manual re-extract required after each revision cycle, causing stale inputs to the workforce model

l4_steps.name: Model staffing ratios by role and operational area
l4_steps.input: Flight frequency forecast, historical headcount-to-output ratios
l4_steps.output: Staffing ratio model by department (ops, cabin crew, ground handling, corporate)
l4_steps.kpi: Ratio deviation ≤5% vs prior year actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR Part 117 duty-time limits constrain crew FTE ratios and are not natively modelled in SuccessFactors; manual adjustments required for each schedule scenario

l4_steps.name: Overlay attrition and turnover projections
l4_steps.input: 3-year attrition history, exit survey data, retirement eligibility register
l4_steps.output: Attrition-adjusted headcount gap model by role and grade
l4_steps.kpi: Attrition forecast accuracy ±2pp vs 12-month rolling actuals
l4_steps.pain_point: Pilot attrition is volatile due to competitor hiring campaigns and Boeing MAX delivery schedule; SuccessFactors demographic model does not ingest external labour market signals

l4_steps.name: Assess certification and type rating requirements
l4_steps.input: Current workforce certification register, planned route and fleet expansions
l4_steps.output: Certification gap analysis covering type ratings, check airmen, and licensed dispatchers
l4_steps.kpi: Zero FAA/EASA non-compliance findings at annual audit
l4_steps.pain_point: 737 MAX type rating lead times of 9–12 months create long procurement cycles; late identification of gaps forces expensive contractor or wet-lease cover

l4_steps.name: Consolidate departmental headcount requests
l4_steps.input: Departmental business plans, headcount request forms
l4_steps.output: Consolidated headcount demand register by department and grade
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of headcount requests submitted via SuccessFactors (zero shadow-spreadsheet submissions)
l4_steps.pain_point: Ground operations departments routinely bypass SuccessFactors and submit requests by email, causing reconciliation delays of 3–5 business days

l4_steps.name: Validate requests against approved operational plan
l4_steps.input: Consolidated headcount demand register, approved flight schedule
l4_steps.output: Validated headcount demand list with business justification scores
l4_steps.kpi: Validation cycle completed ≤5 business days from submission close
l4_steps.pain_point: Schedule volatility during irregular operations invalidates demand validation within weeks of submission; no automated re-trigger exists in SuccessFactors when SkyWORKS schedule changes

l4_steps.name: Run base, upside, and downside scenario models
l4_steps.input: Validated demand list, three schedule scenarios from Amadeus SkySYM
l4_steps.output: Three-scenario headcount model with FTE count and loaded cost estimate per scenario
l4_steps.kpi: Scenario model delivered ≤10 business days from schedule freeze date
l4_steps.pain_point: Custom ETL between AWS Redshift and SuccessFactors introduces 24-hour data latency, reducing scenario responsiveness during rapid schedule changes

l4_steps.name: Submit headcount plan for financial cost review
l4_steps.input: Three-scenario headcount model with FTE cost estimate
l4_steps.output: Headcount cost impact loaded into cost-centre budget in SAP CO
l4_steps.kpi: Headcount cost submission completed ≤2 weeks before annual budget lock date
l4_steps.pain_point: Mid-year headcount additions require supplemental budget approval; SAP CO cost-centre realignment for new positions is manual and error-prone when org structures change

l4_steps.name: Obtain finance approval for headcount envelope
l4_steps.input: Headcount cost model, approved OPEX budget by cost centre
l4_steps.output: Approved or rejected headcount envelope per department with approved FTE ceiling
l4_steps.kpi: Approval decision returned ≤10 business days of submission
l4_steps.pain_point: Executive approval cycles extend by 4–6 weeks during periods of financial pressure such as fuel price spikes, delaying time-to-hire for safety-critical roles

l4_steps.name: Revise and lock headcount plan per finance decision
l4_steps.input: Finance approval decision with department-level adjustments
l4_steps.output: Revised and version-locked headcount plan published to all HR Business Partners
l4_steps.kpi: Revised plan published within 3 business days of finance approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Version control in SuccessFactors Workforce Planning is limited; multiple revision cycles create confusion between HR and Finance on which version constitutes the locked baseline

l4_steps.name: Create approved position records in HRIS
l4_steps.input: Locked headcount plan with approved FTE ceiling by department
l4_steps.output: Approved position records in Employee Central with cost centre, grade, org unit, and FTE flag
l4_steps.kpi: Position creation within 2 business days of plan lock; 100% data quality pass on mandatory fields
l4_steps.pain_point: Employee Central position management requires manual org chart updates that are time-consuming for large cohort hires such as seasonal cabin crew intakes of 200+ headcount

l4_steps.name: Trigger recruitment workflow per approved position
l4_steps.input: Approved position records from Employee Central
l4_steps.output: Job requisitions opened in SuccessFactors Recruiting; JDs published to careers portal
l4_steps.kpi: Time-to-open requisition ≤1 business day; 100% of requisitions linked to an approved position record
l4_steps.pain_point: Pilot and licensed dispatcher requisitions require FAA/EASA qualification screening criteria not pre-built in SuccessFactors Recruiting templates, causing manual customisation per role

l4_steps.name: Confirm headcount actuals against plan at point of hire
l4_steps.input: Offer accepted and onboarding record created in Employee Central
l4_steps.output: Headcount actuals updated; remaining open-position count reconciled to approved ceiling
l4_steps.kpi: Headcount actuals vs plan variance ≤3% at each quarter-end
l4_steps.pain_point: Backfill hires for unexpected attrition routinely consume approved new-hire slots, distorting the plan vs actual comparison and masking net headcount growth

l4_steps.name: Publish monthly headcount actuals vs plan dashboard
l4_steps.input: Live headcount data from Employee Central, open requisition aging report
l4_steps.output: Monthly headcount dashboard showing actuals vs plan, attrition rate, and open-requisition aging
l4_steps.kpi: Dashboard published by Day 5 of each month; plan variance flagged automatically if >5%
l4_steps.pain_point: SuccessFactors People Analytics runs on prior-day data; same-day joiners and leavers in high-volume ops departments are missed, understating attrition in real-time views

l4_steps.name: Conduct mid-year headcount reforecast
l4_steps.input: YTD actuals, updated H2 flight schedule from SkyWORKS, revised attrition forecast
l4_steps.output: Mid-year headcount reforecast with gap-to-plan analysis and recommended actions
l4_steps.kpi: Reforecast submitted ≤15 business days after H1 close; all variances >3% documented with root cause
l4_steps.pain_point: Mid-year schedule changes by Network Planning in SkyWORKS are not automatically signalled to HR, so workforce reforecasts are often triggered 4–6 weeks late

l4_steps.name: Escalate critical headcount gaps to executive committee
l4_steps.input: Reforecast gap analysis exceeding ±5% of plan, operational risk register
l4_steps.output: ExCo escalation report with options: revised hiring authority, freeze, or contractor cover; decision recorded
l4_steps.kpi: Escalation report presented within 5 business days of trigger; resolution decision returned ≤10 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Airline operational staffing shortfalls for pilots and licensed dispatchers carry regulatory consequences under FAR Part 121; delayed escalation has resulted in AOG situations and DOT scrutiny
